faq: What does this tool calculate?
Pixels = ground metres ÷ metres-per-pixel at the given zoom and latitude, under the Web Mercator tile standard (256-pixel tiles, equator circumference scale 156,543.03 m/px at zoom 0).
Which map standard does it use?
The slippy-map Web Mercator standard used by OSM, Google and MapLibre tiles — the convention your screenshots and embeds actually live in.
Can I use this in production GIS?
For display-scale conversions, yes — it is the standard formula. Metric measurement of features belongs to geodesic tools, not pixel counts.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84, the frame web maps and GPS share — tile and pixel systems on this page are defined over it.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — pixels and tiles quantise the world; extra coordinate decimals beyond the cell size are decoration.
North-south versus east-west?
Web Mercator pixels are square on screen and the scale at a point is the same in both directions locally — latitude sets it, direction does not (unlike arcseconds).
Device pixel ratios?
CSS pixels versus device pixels differ on retina screens (×2). State which pixel you mean; this converter speaks CSS/map pixels, the tile standard's unit.
Print maps?
Print has DPI, not zoom — convert via the printed scale bar instead. Pixel logic is screen logic.
Why does latitude matter so much?
Mercator stretches the map vertically toward the poles to keep angles true; pixel ground-size falls by cos(latitude) in compensation.
Fractional pixels?
Features land on fractional pixels constantly — the converter reports decimals; rendering rounds, measurement should not.
The reverse (pixels to ground)?
Map Pixels to Ground Distance is the dedicated return lane.
